utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. I think that we have to discuss a few procedural matters before we start with the rebuttal witnesses. Let me start with the motion filed by Counsel Krajina that we [redacted] [redacted]. The Trial Chamber has decided to grant this motion, and we very much hope that [redacted] will able to come next week as you suggested in your motion. So we will today issue a summons so that [redacted] can come next week, on Monday or Tuesday. Then we have the probative proposal by counsel for Zoran Kupreskic. I wonder whether the Prosecutor has any comments. This relates to the piece of Yugoslav legislation relating to the status of reservists. Any comments from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to be very brief. First of all, good morning to you, Your Honours. I think that this cannot be used as evidence. I don't think that this motion can be used to present some evidence at the Tribunal; it cannot be filed into the file of this case. I'm not sure what Mr. Radovic aims to prove by communicating this piece of legislation. He is not telling us in any way how this definition given by Mr. Radovic has been translated into the Yugoslav legal code. If Mr. Radovic is of the mind that this piece of evidence can be of some utility to him, I think he can inform the Tribunal of this within the framework of his final arguments. But as things stand right now, and in view of the procedures implemented by this Tribunal, I don't think this motion can be accepted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Here we have heard a great deal about the definition of a military, of a military person, and the Prosecutor is trying to prove to the Chamber something that everybody who comes from the former Yugoslavia is clear about: that a reservist is not a military. The former Yugoslav law defines who is who -- who is what, rather. I translated only things that refer to military persons, and what is valuable, and also who is a military. And if I used the text of the criminal law of Yugoslavia, which was at that time valid in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, then it was simply to show the definition as to who is deemed a military, and the definition is -- it transpires quite clear from that definition that a reservist is not a military. Now they want a legal text, naked legal text, to be used as a piece of evidence. That is why I am against it. You should simply bear in mind, when passing your decision, what was defined as a military person by the former criminal law of Yugoslavia, and not to consider somebody as a military only because he is on a list of reservists. The interpretation can be provided only by people from a given legal system, where it is not a general legal system, even though such a general obligation did not exist in the French law, but I believe it did exist in Anglo-Saxon countries. I do not think we have to now translate the law on the former military obligation of the former Yugoslavia, because it is very long, and on the general national defence, one can also conclude who is a military person. All these laws were harmonised as far as the terminology is concerned. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I please answer very briefly to what Mr. Radovic has just said. What is submitted to Your Honours is a question of fact: Who was in combat; who was armed, who was not armed; who was a civilian, who was not a civilian; who was in a state such that he could fight, who was not in a condition to fight. What Mr. Radovic is putting to us is a legal definition, who [sic] has been inscribed for an unknown motive into the Criminal Code of Yugoslavia. This is not a Tribunal for pension funds, who would be in charge of giving some pensions and alimony to ex-military men. In that case, maybe we could resort to a former Yugoslavia legal code. This Tribunal has to judge facts, and in order to appreciate these facts, I don't think this legal document that Mr. Radovic has transmitted to us is of any utility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We should not engage, I think, in a discussion on this particular issue. I think what was suggested by the Prosecutor is right; namely, that we have received this document; you will mention it, I assume, in your closing statement, and it will be taken into account as far as the legal side of the matter is concerned. As for the facts, it will be for the parties to pass on the facts and to show how the facts are presented. Therefore it is not admitted into evidence. It's not evidence, but it will be taken into account by, I assume, Counsel Radovic in his closing statement, and of course, if need be, by the Court when pronouncing on the whole matter, both on the issues of fact and the issues of law. If it is acceptable, we can move on to other procedural matters. Are there any questions which either party would like to raise before we start with the rebuttal witnesses? Yes, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I should like to adduce some documents for the record. These are certified statements of character witnesses for Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic. These are six statements, and I think they all make part of one document, and I should like to seek their admission. Will the usher please help me?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D29/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have some further documents. It is the finding of a ballistics expert, Damir Catiopovic, who testified as to some characteristics of the rifle MGB. These findings were delivered to the Prosecutor in time, and the Prosecutor's Office stated they were accepting the opinion. We did not call this expert witness to testify here. So it was only an expert analysis of the rifle and as regards two features: one is the firing of the rifle, and the second is the type of ammunition used for that rifle. I should like to adduce this into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one thing. We're not at all opposed to the submission to the Tribunal of the expert's report on the MGB rifle. I -- in fact, this document had already been admitted into the case file. As for the affidavits, for six affidavits which have just been communicated by Mrs. Slokovic-Glumac, if we can make sure that witness's statements are, in fact, linked to the character and personality of the accused, and I would like to be granted a few moments to make sure of that. Even though right now we do not find ourselves in the framework of Rule 94 ter of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, we are not opposed to the submission of these documents, and I don't believe we will ever be opposed to the communication of these documents, but please leave me until tomorrow so that I can give a final decision about these particular documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. I think this is a very sensible suggestion. So we'll put off this question until tomorrow. The Prosecutor will carefully examine the six affidavits, and then they will let us know whether or not they object to the admission into evidence. Whereas the other document has been -- since there's no objection, it will be admitted into evidence. I wonder if we can get a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D30/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have yet another batch of documents. These are documents

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: [redacted]. These are documents which my learned friend, Mr. Radovic, used when he checked the credibility of the witness, and all these documents were rejected because they had not been translated into English. [redacted] shows that he did not deny the existence of these documents or events related to their origin. The only question, contested question, was that there was no English translation. So we should like to suggest that they all be admitted as one batch of documents and -- just a moment. Sorry. They were refused as D3/1 to D8/1 on the same grounds; that is, that there was no English translation. I should now like these documents and their translations to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Did the Prosecution have an opportunity to take a look at these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Well, no, Your Honour. In fact, I'm not sure what we're talking about. So before saying anything, I would like to have the opportunity to have a look at them. Could I be granted some time to have a look at them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So until tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, until tomorrow, please, Mr. President. I will then give you our decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: It is so decided.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibits D31/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have before me a list of exhibits relative to the accused Dragan Papic, which were given by the Prosecutor on the 16th of July, 1999, and the first name on the list is Mehmed Ahmic. It is a statement he made to the investigators of the International Tribunal. I did hand over the statement to the Tribunal, but I forgot to ask that it be admitted into evidence. So may I do that now? If I can do it now, I should like to tender it into evidence, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Puliselic, it is admitted into evidence, then. Do we have a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was D1/5. There are two versions of it, in Croatian and in English. So D1/5, and D1/5A for the Croatian and English versions. Of the 28th -- it was on -- the 21st of August, 1998, was when I tendered them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any other housekeeping matters, procedural matters? None? Now, before we start with the rebuttal witnesses, let me try to do some planning. We have now received a list of rebuttal witnesses. There are five. I understand Mr. McLeod will be called next Monday, on the 4th of October. Then on top of that we have -- now we will summon a Court witness, as a Court witness, (redacted). I gather there were no rejoinder witnesses. The Defence counsel are not going to call any rejoinder witnesses. So that means by -- Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic's Defence counsel have been thinking about two witnesses, and we were planning to call two witnesses, but we shall decide after we have heard the Prosecution's rebuttal witnesses; that is, if it turns out to be necessary, there are two names, and we should supply them to the Prosecution today. We have not spoken to them yet, but they have to do with rebuttal witnesses for the Prosecution. They will come here in due course. However, we really do not know if we shall need to call them or not, because we think that after this examination, cross-examination, it will no longer be necessary. So we should like to defer our decision until the conclusion of the testimonies of rebuttal witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Vladimir Santic's counsel is also planning to call one witness, but whether it will be necessary to do so shall be decided by us after we have heard the Prosecution's witness; that is, as my learned friend Slokovic-Glumac has already said, it may be during the cross-examination, or even before, that we shall decide that we shall not need this witness. So will you please take note of this. However, I shall know the name of that witness today and I shall duly inform the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence of the accused Vlatko Kupreskic is planning also to call the accused Vlatko Kupreskic to give his statement, to answer questions with reference to the new evidence about to be produced by the Prosecution. We have notified the Prosecutor about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Is it for sure? Are you planning whether or not to call him? You have decided to call him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: We have decided. We have decided, Mr. President. We have decided so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you allow me a very brief remark on what has just been said by Mr. Krajina? In this rebuttal phase, the Prosecution aims to put its stress on one particular element of fact, a very precise element of fact; i.e., the place where Dzenana and Fata Pezer were found when they were; first of all, injured, then killed. Within this rebuttal phase we are not going to touch any other subject. In these circumstances, I cannot understand why, within the framework of the rejoinder, it is planned that Vlatko Kupreskic will be called to the stand when he, in fact, was not present. He was not present at the place where the victims I had talked about were injured. So maybe we're going to know right now that Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic was, in fact, present, but unless this is proven to us, we don't see that it could be of any use to have Mr. Kupreskic come to the stand. I don't think it would be in conformity with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal to hear once again the accused Vlatko Kupreskic, who has had a long opportunity to give his views on this case. Then I would like to make a remark on the order of appearance of the witnesses. This is matter of information to you, Your Honours, and to inform the counsels of defence for the order of appearance. A document was communicated to this Chamber on September 20th, 1999. It appears on this document that there's been a change, rather, in this document. The first witness which will come before you will be the witness which comes second, and then we'll have Mr. Howard Tucker coming third. The fourth witness, or, rather, the third witness, will be the fourth witness of the list. Then the fourth witness will be the first witness appearing on the list. So there's been a slight change in the order of appearance. Another thing I would like to inform you about -- and I think you know about this already, Mr. McLeod -- the witness who appears as witness number 5 will only come next Monday, for personal reasons. As for witness number 4, we would ask to be allowed to have him come in only on Thursday, because we have to have some time to talk to him and prepare him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: I do apologise, but as regards what has just been said by the Prosecutor, from the documents handed us over by the Prosecution and relative to the reconstruction of the events in Ahmici, conducted again by the Prosecution, it is quite feasible that the witnesses, and especially Witness Q, described, among other things, the area which is in the immediate vicinity of Vlatko Kupreskic's house in Ahmici, and they describe both the area, the lay of the land, and the spinney, and things like that, for a long time. We believe that Vlatko Kupreskic is a man who grew up in the area, is quite qualified, and that he's a man who can best portray this area to the Tribunal and respond to claims of the witnesses who spoke about the area and everything else that happened there. I do not think it will be a long testimony. It would merely be a response to those witness statements which the Prosecution heard during the reconstruction of the events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will pass on this matter and make a ruling on whether or not the -- it is admissible for the accused Vlatko Kupreskic to be heard again as a rejoinder witness, at the end of the rebuttal witnesses. So at that point only shall we decide this matter. So we defer any decision on the matter until after the rebuttal witnesses have all been heard. We can now then move on and start with rebuttal witnesses if there's no other matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, our first witness has asked for protection measures. He has asked to testify within a closed session. The Defence counsels have been informed of this this morning. They have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We'll move into a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 1.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of September, 1999, at 1.00 p.m.
